strategies.description: Bahrain is a high degradation circuit. Rear-limited with abrasive surface causing high tyre wear. The pit lane is relatively standard at ~22.5s loss.
strategies.typical_strategy: Two-stop: SOFT(15-18) → HARD(20-22) → MEDIUM(17-20) or one-stop MEDIUM(25) → HARD(32)
key_factors: long straights favor hard tyres late
undercut is powerful due to high deg

strategies.description: Verstappen dominated with a standard two-stop. High degradation meant one-stop was not viable for frontrunners. SC did not deploy.
strategies.notes: Leclerc tried extending stint 1 but suffered significant deg drop-off.

strategies.description: Monaco is a low degradation street circuit where track position is paramount. Overtaking is nearly impossible, making strategy mostly about tyre management. Pit loss is very high at ~24s.
strategies.typical_strategy: One-stop: MEDIUM(35-40) → HARD(38-43) or HARD(40) → MEDIUM(38). Some attempt no-stop on HARD.

strategies.description: Leclerc won his home race from pole. Classic Monaco strategy — maintain track position, one-stop, manage tyres. No real opportunity to undercut due to pit loss.
strategies.notes: Late SC bunched the field but positions held.

strategies.description: Silverstone is a high-speed circuit with high energy corners causing significant front-left tyre wear. Weather variability is the biggest strategy wildcard.
strategies.typical_strategy: Two-stop: SOFT(16-18) → MEDIUM(18-20) → SOFT(14-16) or one-stop MEDIUM(26) → HARD(26)

strategies.description: Monza is the lowest downforce circuit on the calendar. Low tyre degradation due to few slow corners, but very high pit loss (~25s) due to long pit lane.
strategies.typical_strategy: One-stop: MEDIUM(24-28) → HARD(25-29) or even attempt zero-stop on HARD

strategies.description: Singapore is a high degradation street circuit with high SC probability (68%). The street surface is aggressive on tyres and the race is physically demanding.
strategies.typical_strategy: Two-stop: SOFT(15) → MEDIUM(22) → HARD(25) with SC-dependent variants. SC almost always deploys.

strategies.description: Spa is a long lap with varied corners. Low pit loss (~21s) and moderate degradation. Weather can change rapidly with the Ardennes microclimate.
strategies.typical_strategy: One-stop: MEDIUM(22) → HARD(22) or two-stop with SOFT start if weather stays dry
key_factors: low pit loss relative to lap time

strategies.description: Jeddah is a high-speed street circuit with very high SC probability (65%). Barrier-lined track means incidents are common. Medium-high degradation.
strategies.typical_strategy: One or two-stop: MEDIUM(18-20) → HARD(30-32) or SOFT(14) → HARD(20) → MEDIUM(16) if SC expected

strategies.description: Hungaroring is a tight, twisty circuit where overtaking is very difficult — like Monaco without the glamour. High degradation due to slow corners and hot conditions.
strategies.typical_strategy: Two-stop: SOFT(18) → MEDIUM(26) → SOFT(26) or MEDIUM(30) → HARD(40) one-stop

strategies.description: COTA is a balanced circuit with varied corners. Medium degradation with bumpy surface causing tyre vibrations. Standard 56-lap race.
strategies.typical_strategy: Two-stop: MEDIUM(18) → HARD(20) → SOFT(18) or one-stop MEDIUM(28) → HARD(28)

strategies.description: Baku is a street circuit with the longest straight on the calendar. Very high SC probability (72%). Low degradation on most compounds but tyre failures from debris possible.
strategies.typical_strategy: One-stop: HARD(24) → MEDIUM(27) or two-stop MEDIUM(15) → HARD(20) → SOFT(16) gambling on late SC

strategies.description: The undercut works by pitting before a rival to gain a tyre advantage. Fresh tyres are typically 1-3 seconds per lap faster. The driver behind pits first, does fast out-laps on new tyres, and comes out ahead when the rival eventually pits.
key_factors: pit loss must be overcome by pace advantage
driver ahead can respond by counter-pitting

strategies.description: The overcut works by staying out while a rival pits. The driver staying out benefits from clear air and a lighter car (more fuel burned) to set fast laps before pitting. Most effective when the track rubbers in or when out-lap traffic is heavy.

Safety car periods are the most impactful strategy events. Pit loss under SC is reduced by ~15 seconds as the field circulates slowly. Teams that pit during SC gain a 'free' stop. Those who don't pit gain track position but on older tyres.
key_factors: track position vs fresh tyres trade-off

strategies.description: Virtual Safety Car reduces pit loss by about 10 seconds compared to normal racing. Less impactful than full SC but still creates a strategic opportunity. The field maintains gaps proportionally rather than bunching.

Rain forces a switch to intermediate or wet tyres. Timing the switch is critical — too early means slow laps on a drying track, too late means aquaplaning risk. Crossover point between slicks and inters varies by 3-5 seconds depending on rain intensity.
Mercedes historically tends to overcut, preferring track position and clear air. They manage tyres well in long stints and often extend stints beyond the expected window.
Red Bull historically favors the undercut, often pitting aggressively to gain track position. Under Verstappen, they are decisive and rarely wait. Strong in traffic management.

Ferrari has historically been inconsistent with strategy, sometimes making conservative calls that cost positions. However, they have strong race pace and can recover from suboptimal strategy through raw speed.
